summary: A satirical article mocking the market boom in eco-friendly and sustainable products from September 2023 to April 2024. It uses quotes from fictional or humorous figures to skewer greenwashing, infinitely recyclable bottles, pricey green goods, disintegrating biodegradable items, eco-fashion, organic food claims, and the circular economy. The central question is whether these products save the planet or just profit margins.
one_line: Satirical piece lampooning greenwashing and the eco-friendly product boom across packaging, bottles, fashion, organic food, and the circular economy.
key_facts: The article says consumers have been swept up in the sustainability marketing craze from September 2023 onward.
On October 5, 2023, Jane Dough, CEO of EcoMasquerade Inc., was quoted saying that if a package is green or says 'natural,' it sells.
Infinity-recyclable water bottles were introduced at the Lucrative Innovations Conference on November 15, 2023.
Keynote speaker Bob Greenroots claimed at the Lucrative Innovations Conference that owning one of the bottles 'erases your carbon footprint for life.'
On December 3, 2023, Sir Cashington said at a press conference that green packaging costs more and that 'Green is the new gold!'
Environmental blogger Tina Tumbleleaf said on January 8, 2024 that her eco-friendly smartphone case started disintegrating quickly.
Fashion commentator Chic McFad noted on February 1, 2024 that a dress equivalent to 50 plastic bottles sells at a markup.
The article contrasts a $200 recycled bottle dress with a $20 cotton one.
As of March 3, 2024, supermarkets reported a 500% increase in sales of products labeled 'organic.'
Self-proclaimed nutrition guru Bronson Peachfuzz claimed eating organic adds twenty years to your life and cures most ailments, citing no sources.
Circular economy skeptic Jack Naysayer said on April 17, 2024 that the circular economy is 'a roundabout where all exits lead to profit town.'
The article closes by questioning whether eco-friendly products save the planet or just consumers' faces, noting settlements on Mars are being planned.
